description: 16 March 1988. Between 3,200 and 5,000 killed and 7,000-10,000 injured, mostly civilians. UN investigation concluded mustard gas plus unidentified nerve agents. Part of the Anfal campaign, in which an estimated 182,000 Kurds were killed.

aspect: Thirty-eight years later, the mental health numbers
description: A 2026 Frontiers in Psychiatry study found PTSD in 79% of survivors, depression or anxiety in 65%, and severe somatic symptoms, with women and those of lower socioeconomic status most affected.
energy_note: Four fifths of a town, still, after thirty-eight years.

aspect: THE GENERATIONAL FINDING - and it is not genetic
description: A cross-generational study across three cohorts - victimised as adults, victimised as children, and not affected - found all three, including those never exposed, reported elevated depression, PTSD symptom severity and sleep disturbance. The authors note the cohorts were not genetically related, so critical life events transfer to the next generation without genetic overlap.
energy_note: Inherited without a gene in sight.
source_name: J Affect Disord, cross-generational Halabja study
notes: This is the single most useful row in the dataset for the question of whether transmission is genetic. Answer: partly, and it does not need to be.

aspect: Women's outcomes, and the neglect of them
description: Ovarian and cervical cancer, infertility, disabled or stillborn babies. Halabja women have publicly complained of neglect; there are few female medical specialists in or near the town to treat reproductive problems and cancers.
energy_note: A specific harm, and no specialist within reach of it.

aspect: Birth defects and cancer in the region afterwards
description: Preliminary surveys of the affected region showed increased rates of cancer and birth defects in the years following, alongside documented higher rates of infertility and miscarriage in exposed populations.
energy_note: A birth rate that carries the attack forward.

aspect: No services exist for the specific injury
description: There are no dedicated health services for sulfur mustard survivors in Iraqi Kurdistan, though registered chemical-weapons-exposed patients receive a life annuity and social benefits. Money, but no clinic.
money_note: Out-of-region private care for a condition with no local service.
energy_note: Compensated in cash for a treatment that does not exist.

aspect: The justice dimension does not close either
description: Survivors continue to seek recognition and accountability decades on. An unresolved legal status keeps the event permanently present rather than historical, which is itself a documented barrier to symptom resolution.
energy_note: It cannot become the past until someone says so officially.
